problem: Image-relative topological navigation controllers (GNM, ViNT, SPTM) condition on a subgoal image tied to the agent's pose and embodiment. They fail when the route must differ from the prior trajectory (new goals, shortcuts, reverse travel) and when the mapping and execution embodiments differ.
motivation: Objects are a property of the map, so they are invariant to pose, embodiment and trajectory. Conditioning control on the objects visible in the current view removes the need to retrieve a subgoal image and to solve image matching inside the controller. It also avoids the quadratically larger cross-embodiment training data that mapping-execution invariance would otherwise need.
key_idea: Learn an object-relative controller conditioned only on a 'WayObject Costmap', the current view's object masks painted with their path-length-to-goal from a relative 3D scene graph, with no RGB input and no subgoal image.
insight: Grounding subgoal conditioning in objects rather than images fixes several image-relative weaknesses. Object-relative ObjectReact reaches 21.74 SPL on Alt Goal against 2.17 for GNM, and its height-change drop is 3.04 SPL against 48.49. An off-the-shelf real-world GNM performs similarly to the sim-trained GNM, so the gap comes from the representation rather than the training data. Dropping RGB improves results (Imitate SPL 71.20 vs 63.61), suggesting RGB causes overfitting to training instances. Relative 3D edges beat 2D Delaunay edges (Shortcut SPL 59.61 vs 19.23). Remaining weakness on hard tasks is mostly perception: results with ground-truth instances are far higher.
method: Relative 3D scene graph mapping: SAM2 masks are object nodes with a 3D point from Depth Anything monocular depth and a fixed focal length; intra-image edges connect all object pairs weighted by 3D Euclidean distance.
Inter-image edges: SuperPoint+LightGlue matches keypoints between consecutive frames (3 previous frames) and segment correspondences are set by keypoint counts; edge weight 0, which merges the nodes.

Execution-time localization and planning (RoboHop style): FastSAM segments the query, which is matched to a submap around the GT-localized map image; Dijkstra path lengths to the goal node are assigned, taking the minimum over multiple matches; a tracking mechanism over 8 history frames fills unlocalized segments, and unmatched segments get an outlier cost.

WayObject Costmap: per-image normalized path lengths are rescaled to [1,L] and given a D=8 sine-cosine encoding; the encoding is multiplied by the binary masks to form an H×W×D image (85×64) that needs no RGB.

ObjectReact controller: a GNM-based architecture with a single custom ResNet goal encoder taking the D-channel costmap; it predicts 10 BEV waypoints and the last one is converted to clipped velocities.
Training: shortest-path demonstrations from HM3D IIN-train (145 scenes × 20 episodes); costmaps come from simulator instances and depth, with 30% of segments randomly replaced by the outlier cost.

setting.backbone: GNM-style ResNet controller with a custom WayObject-Costmap goal encoder (trained from scratch); perception uses frozen SAM2/FastSAM, SuperPoint-LightGlue, Depth Anything and CLIP
setting.training_data: Simulator shortest-path trajectories from HM3Dv0.2 IIN-train: 145 scenes × 20 uniformly sampled episodes, split 80/20 train/val; sim-only, with 30% random outlier-cost augmentation.
setting.observation: Monocular RGB (120° FOV, 320×240 for mapping/execution, 85×65 for the controller) converted to a WayObject Costmap; the controller receives no RGB by default
setting.action_space: Predicted 10 BEV waypoints converted to continuous linear (0-0.05 m/s in sim) and angular (±0.1 rad/s) velocities
setting.privileged: GT localization (closest map image index) in all experiments; the goal node is chosen using the GT goal segmentation mask; GT instance segmentation and depth for training costmaps and for the ablation-table costmaps; oracle stop.

numbers.eval_set_note: IIN-val, 36 scenes with one episode each, with invalid episodes excluded per task (6 removed for Imitate); 72 runs over two sensor heights (1.3m, 0.4m); inferred perception (FastSAM + SuperPoint-LightGlue)

results: With inferred perception, ObjectReact roughly matches sim-trained GNM on Imitate (59.08 vs 57.58 SPL) but far outperforms it on Alt Goal (21.74 vs 2.17), Shortcut (23.08 vs 7.69) and Reverse (26.67 vs 11.60). Under a robot-height change, its SPL changes by only 3.04 versus 48.49 for GNM. With GT-instance costmaps it beats RoboHop and PixNav controllers on Imitate, Shortcut and Reverse (e.g. Shortcut SPL 59.61 vs 48.03 for RoboHop and 19.23 for PixNav), while Alt Goal is slightly below the RGB variant and RoboHop/PixNav are clearly behind it.
limitations: Perception (segmentation and matching) is the bottleneck: absolute performance on hard tasks with inferred perception is still low, and the setup relies on GT localization and oracle stop.
Static map assumption with no exploration; large scene changes or dynamic objects break object connectivity, and floor/ceiling nodes create planning shortcuts that need CLIP-based removal.
Sim-to-real gap: shortest-path training leaves little obstacle margin and causes collisions; no history context; real-world evidence is only qualitative videos.
